tb21_profile.skill: Implement a published sampling algorithm (Gilks & Wild 1992 ARS) from its paper description: tangent/chord hulls of a log-concave density, envelope rejection with a squeeze test, adaptive refinement, log-concavity violation detection, plus a self-written stochastic test harness that compares samples to known truth.
tb21_profile.domain: R language / numerical statistics / Monte Carlo random-variate generation and density evaluation; also R toolchain install.
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec (algorithm from a paper) with modular API design, input validation, error handling, and author-your-own PASS/FAIL statistical test suite.

verifier_notes: task_005309_e36db87c (TMax, Metropolis-Hastings sampler in Rust + regression test against the analytical posterior mean) is graded FREE. It is one of the closest TMax matches on skill, but the grade is plausible: its checks are file/substring-shaped, so it is excluded from final_top10 and from per_source in favour of graded equivalents. task_04497 (Terminal-Lego two-sample KS test) is also FREE and excluded for the same reason. No grade I checked looked wrong: scientific-computing_20260421_155939_001 is graded weak but its suite does assert on sample moments, so 'weak' understates it slightly; it is still safely non-FREE.

TMax-15K.reason: Implements Monte Carlo rejection sampling from scratch, then must prove statistical correctness and run a convergence test - the ARS core loop and its validation.
Rejection sampling against a given PDF, derive the analytical CDF yourself, then score samples with a KS distance. Same accept/reject reasoning plus truth comparison.
Write a Metropolis-Hastings sampler and validate its sample statistics against the exact analytical Beta-Binomial posterior - the 'test stochastic output against known truth' requirement.
Build a lightweight MCMC sampler in pure NumPy/SciPy instead of calling PyMC/Stan - same 'implement the sampler yourself, no library shortcut' constraint.
Generate samples from a known posterior via MCMC and validate them analytically as a gold-standard dataset; same sample-and-verify pipeline, less algorithmic depth.
Fix reproducibility and numerical stability in an MCMC sampler and measure sample-vs-truth fit by KL divergence; exercises sampler numerics and stochastic validation.
Debug adaptive step-size control in a stochastic integrator so its samples match a target Gaussian - adaptive refinement plus distributional checking, different mechanism.
Replace C rand() with a statistically rigorous generator for bootstrap resampling; teaches that RNG quality changes the sampled distribution, which ARS depends on.
Generate samples from a specified Gaussian mixture and gate them on a KS distance against a baseline; sampling plus distributional acceptance test, wrapped in an HTTP service.
Writes an R script that fits a curve and then analytically validates and classifies the result; nearest TMax task that is actually authored in R with pinned checks.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Write a numeric C++ program, run it, then run the supplied validator and show every computed value passed - compute-then-validate-against-truth, but arithmetic is trivial.
Starter numeric C++ program may be wrong; must produce a validation report and artifact manifest. Debug-a-numeric-routine-then-report, closest RTS gets to the test-harness requirement.
Author a ShellSpec test project that validates a function's behaviour and run the suite - the only RTS task about writing your own tests rather than running someone else's.
Implement an N-Queens solver as a CLI with validated flags; algorithm-from-spec plus argument validation, no statistics anywhere.
Compute column means over a ROOT TTree - scientific numerical data handling, but a single aggregate rather than an algorithm.
Babashka script defining two named functions over numeric input with a checksum check; modular-functions-plus-self-check shape, trivial math.
Produce a report confirming computed square roots match a reference dataset; same compute-then-prove-correct genre as the ARS test function.
Implement an algorithm in an unfamiliar language (ARM64 asm) plus a build file - transfers only the 'work in a language you rarely write' pressure.
ARM64 program computing an average with a Makefile; numeric output in an unfamiliar language, no modelling or validation depth.
Implement a new mode from a written REQUIREMENTS.md while preserving existing behaviour; implement-from-spec discipline only, wrong domain entirely.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Implement Newton's method for integer sqrt as a Forth word and run it on given inputs - iterative numerical algorithm written from its mathematical description in an unfamiliar language.
Enumerate twin primes to 1e8 and apply the standard extrapolation correction - implement a published estimation formula and produce a numeric estimate.
Word-frequency analysis demonstrating Zipf's law with a log-log distribution plot; empirical distribution fitting, but no generator to build.
Compute observed fraction of the 26^n space and Shannon entropy in bits and bits-per-character; quantitative summary statistics against a theoretical maximum.
Show 32-bit Posits beat IEEE floats on a numerical problem in Julia - floating-point accuracy reasoning, which ARS needs for log-density arithmetic.
Generate random numbers three different ways under GraalVM native-image; only the RNG-plumbing half of sampling, no target distribution.
N-Queens solver with -n and -f flags; algorithm-from-spec plus CLI argument handling, unrelated subject matter.
Build a pytest suite with conftest.py that runs from two directories - authoring a working test harness, which is requirement 2 of the ARS task.
Join two CSVs and compute combined area statistics; numeric aggregation over tabular data, nothing stochastic.
Profile a PyTorch model's parameter statistics to two output files; statistical reporting of a model, no algorithm to implement.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: patsy is the Python port of R's statistical formula language; fixing dmatrix means reasoning about R-style model specification and design matrices.
generate_uid is not uniformly or cryptographically random - diagnosing why a generator's output distribution is not what it claims, the ARS log-concavity-check instinct.
NCD implementation gives wrong values and fails a symmetry property test; fix a published algorithm until a mathematical invariant holds.
wait_random_exponential ignores its min bound - a bounded random variate generator producing values outside its declared support.
BaseProvider._random_int breaks when max is supplied; range/domain validation of a random integer generator, the input-checking half of the ARS spec.
Missing 2D residuals case in dask.array.linalg.lstsq - match a numpy reference implementation's numerical output exactly.
Maintainability Index formula computed incorrectly; transcribe a published numeric formula faithfully into code.
precise batch-norm statistics are not accumulated correctly - running estimation of mean and variance over a stream of samples.
Generator seeding is broken, so sampled output is not reproducible; reproducibility of a stochastic routine is what makes the ARS tests testable.
Wrong SQL names emitted for StdDevSamp and VarSamp; sample-statistics vocabulary only, no numerical reasoning at all.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: bernoulli sampling is wrong for p=1e-10 because float32 uniforms only resolve 2^-23; exactly the float-precision trap an envelope sampler hits in the tails.
Replace rejection sampling with construction that satisfies the filter by design - requires understanding rejection-sampling acceptance rates and when they collapse.
A fake Random disagrees with the real Random when sampling; validating one sampler against a reference implementation is the ARS test-function problem.
MCMC returns no samples when the model has only deterministic sites; debugging a sampler's site bookkeeping in a Bayesian sampling library.
Implement SampleMP.process_counts from a written spec - add a new method to a sampling measurement API, implement-from-spec inside a library.
Hankel functions lose accuracy for large imaginary arguments; special-function numerics of the same family as the log-densities and gamma terms ARS evaluates.
A strategy's code does not match the published paper's description of its random 50-50 comparison; reconcile implementation with the source paper, as Gilks & Wild demands.
Attach a prior to a linear mean function so MCMC over GP hyperparameters works; probabilistic-model plumbing in the same statistical stack.
ARX forecast residual variance is not what the model implies; verify a statistical model's output against its analytical expectation.
distributions.py indexes Qobj.data with a pre-v5 API; numerical-library maintenance in a scientific stack, little algorithmic transfer.

Terminal-Lego-15k.reason: Implement inverse-transform sampling for an exponential density from uniforms only, then report sample mean/sd against the theoretical mean/sd and write samples to a file.
Build a normal-distribution generator from Math.random alone; transforming uniforms into a target density without a library is the same core move as ARS.
Write R that uses tryCatch properly - the exact idiom ARS needs for rejecting invalid inputs and signalling non-log-concave densities.
Remove modulo bias from $RANDOM using rejection sampling and then show the output distribution is actually uniform - accept/reject plus distributional verification.
Modular Python module computing streaming mean, variance, skewness and kurtosis; the modular-statistical-components-with-tests shape the ARS grader asks for.
R package install fails on a missing system header; fix with apt then install.packages via Rscript - the 'install R if not already available' half of the task.
Cryptographic RNG within a range using rejection sampling to avoid bias; same discard-and-retry loop, security rather than statistical framing.
Efficient weighted-die data structure for sampling from a discrete pmf; building a fast sampler for an arbitrary given distribution.
Weighted random selection of k items without replacement with correct per-item probabilities; probability-correct sampling, discrete and non-adaptive.
Build a full R modelling pipeline that trains and exports a predictive model; real multi-file R engineering, but statistics-lite and not a sampler.

CalibForge.reason: Implement an HMC sampler that accepts an arbitrary (possibly unnormalized) target log-probability and returns samples - the same contract, the same gradient-of-log-density machinery, as ARS.
Adaptive Gauss-Kronrod quadrature: subdivide where the local error estimate is worst, stay robust on nasty integrands - ARS's adaptive hull refinement in integration form.
Hybrid root-finder combining bracketing guarantees with derivative-driven Newton steps; ARS builds its upper hull from exactly these tangent-line intersections.
Implement GP regression from Rasmussen & Williams (2006) Ch.2 including log-marginal-likelihood optimisation; implement-a-published-method-from-its-text, same genre and depth.
Implement distance correlation from Szekely, Rizzo & Bakirov (2007) from scratch; translate a cited statistics paper into correct code.
C library for regularized incomplete gamma P/Q, gamma, and their inverses - the numerics behind distribution CDFs and quantiles that a sampler's checks rest on.
Adaptive quadrature to a requested tolerance on sharply peaked and near-singular integrands; the same envelope-refinement-until-tolerance control loop.
Diagnose a Metropolis-Hastings sampler for a Normal mean/precision posterior so it recovers the right answer; sampler correctness judged statistically, pinned tests.
Adams-Bashforth-Moulton PECE with Milne's-device step control implemented from its mathematical description; error-estimate-driven adaptation, different subject.
Port an R survival-analysis script to Python lifelines; requires reading real statistical R, but the algorithm is library-supplied rather than implemented.

final_top10.reason: Implement a sampler that takes an arbitrary unnormalized target log-density and emits correct samples - the identical interface and the identical log-density machinery.
Write Monte Carlo rejection sampling from scratch, then prove statistical correctness and convergence - ARS's accept/reject loop plus its validation requirement.
Rejection sampling from a given PDF, derive the analytical CDF by hand, then score the samples by KS distance against it.
Inverse-transform sampler for a named density using uniforms only, with empirical mean/sd checked against the theoretical values and samples written out.
Metropolis-Hastings sampler validated against the exact analytical posterior - the 'compare stochastic output to known truth' test design ARS requires.
Adaptive Gauss-Kronrod quadrature that refines where its error estimate is worst and survives hard integrands; ARS's adaptive envelope refinement in another guise.
Bracketed root-finder with derivative-driven Newton steps and guaranteed convergence - ARS's upper hull is built from these tangent intersections.
Implement GP regression straight from Rasmussen & Williams Ch.2; same genre as implementing Gilks & Wild from the 1992 paper, same depth.
Implement distance correlation from the 2007 paper from scratch - turning a cited statistics paper into correct, testable code.
C implementation of regularized incomplete gamma and its inverse: the distribution-function numerics an ARS log-concavity and normalisation check depends on.

notes: CalibForge clearly beats the v1 pool here: it holds five of the final ten, including the single best match (HMC sampler from a target log-density) and the whole implement-a-published-numerical-method genre that TMax lacks. Terminal-Lego contributes the other new win, task_09244, an inverse-transform sampler validated against theoretical moments. Recursive-Task-Synthesis has NO defensible candidate for this task - its whole shortlist is number-guessing games and Clojure EDN chores, and a words/regex sweep for monte carlo, distribution, sampling, statistic, probability and variance across all 37,484 returned nothing statistical. Its ten entries are the honest best (compute-then-validate numeric chores) and all score 2. TerminalWorld is nearly as thin; only tw_621404 (Newton's method in Forth) is a real algorithm-implementation task, and several of its better-looking hits are FREE. Two close TMax/Lego matches were dropped for being FREE-graded: task_005309_e36db87c (MH sampler in Rust with an analytical-posterior regression test) and task_04497 (two-sample KS test). If the merge step wants a FREE-tolerant variant, those two would rank around final positions 5-8 on content. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench lose on task_form as expected; Rebench is the stronger of the two here because jax/numpyro/hypothesis give genuine sampler-correctness debugging, whereas SWE-Smith's best is patsy (R formula language) at rank 1.
